newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No Brazil complaints so far about Argentine wheat.
newsitem.headline: No Brazil complaints so far about Argentine wheat.

text.p: Brazil's Wheat Millers Association (Abitrigo) has asked mills to submit details of any complaints they may have over the quality of new crop Argentine wheat but has so far received no replies, an official said.
"I have asked all the mills, if you have any complaints about Argentine wheat, let us know. But so far we have received not one claim," said Antenor Barros Leal, Abitrigo president.

Millers said there was concern over the quality of Argentine wheat following rains which affected quality and led to about one million tonnes of feedgrain quality wheat which millers fear may be blended into higher quality product.

Leal said he had written to Argentine Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola at the end of last year offering to sign an agreement in which Abitrigo would supply the Argentine government with information on the quality of Argentine wheat.
So far about 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat have already arrived in Brazil out of total purchases to-date estimated at around 1.5 million tonnes, millers said.
"We have had no complaints yet, just general comments. But to comment is something, to prove it is another," Leal said.

Brazil has been expected to buy up to six million tonnes from its Mercosul partner and the slow rate of purchases is due to government-sponsored auctions of domestic wheat which have resulted in the sale of one million tonnes, Leal said.
"I think the Argentines have been very surprised as they didn't believe that the moves by the Brazilian government to sell domestic wheat would succeed," Leal said.
"Now I think the Argentines are a bit worried," he added.
Brazilian millers are also considering other origins, and Leal said he was planning to visit the U.S., Canada and Germany on a fact-finding visit in the very near future.
